summary: The comment section reads as a confessional, not a music review. Viewers treat จางหาย as autobiography and respond by posting their own long-form breakup stories — several of the most-liked comments run 80-200 words about an ex they never got over, one about a partner lost to cancer. The second-largest cluster is career pride: viewers list everything Goy did herself (wrote lyrics and melody, sang, directed the MV) and frame her as an all-round talent rather than an actress who released a song. A third cluster reads the MV as a coded message to her real ex-partner Nicky, decoding specific shots (the football scene, the first book) and openly asking the pair to reunite. Lyric-quoting and timestamp comments show repeat listening. A visible minority arrived from the TV show The Wall Song rather than from the channel itself.

audience_signals: Parasocial investment in Goy's real-life relationship is the single strongest engagement driver — viewers know the ex by name and read shots as evidence
The comment section functions as a safe space for personal confession; the most-liked comments are long first-person stories, not compliments
Long-tenure fanbase that tracks her across acting, stage, writing and YouTube — repeated 'ภูมิใจในตัวพี่ก้อย' framing signals ownership, not casual viewing
Terrestrial TV exposure (The Wall Song) imports viewers who did not know the song was hers — a proven top-of-funnel outside YouTube
Audience is protective: several comments ask her to prioritise self-love over the reunion narrative other fans push
content_requests: A live performance of the song / hear her sing it at a concert
The duet version with Hai from The Wall Song released as its own track
A reaction video from the Friendsfly friend group, especially Vee
More original songs written by her
